rv.q: Speaking generally, though, “Big Fish” only works if it accepts everything told by Edward Bloom as truth, at least in the storyteller’s eyes and that’s where this choppy, strident and overly stereotypical production struggles.
This production will make you laugh, cry several times but in the end, will make you think of those people in your life you hold dear.

Despite the occasional flash of ridiculous brilliance (rhyming “laughing gas” with “pain in the a--,” for example) and the odd philosophical thought (is life really just a series of “minor triumphs and major disappointments?”), “Big Fish” is no big deal.
I think this is the best version of this musical I have ever seen.
Marriott's 'Big Fish' is a magical night of theater not to be missed.
For those looking for a heartfelt musical about family in an intimate setting, this would be a good fit for you.

Like a welcome folk album to soothe the cacophony of winter 2023’s angsty soundtrack, this understated, not oft-produced, Henry Godinez -directed gem is a warm cup of cocoa reminding everyone in the room that consciously doing the best one can results in lives well lived.
But the theatergoer who enjoys a sincerely performed, beautifully told story about the relationships between real people will be greatly rewarded.
Elements of magical realism elevate “Big Fish” from a rote story of father-son tension into a grand adventure.
Marriott Theatre’s sluggish and uninspired current revival, directed by Henry Godinez, gave me some insights.

The current mounting of the Broadway musical Big Fish at Marriott Theatre is an example of all three.
This kind of larger-than-life magical entertainment is why we love attending the Marriott Lincolnshire Theater.
